name: O. Reg. 213/91: Construction Projects
description: The Construction Projects regulation made under the Occupational Health and Safety Act — the prescriptive rule book for every construction project in Ontario, and the regulation an Ontario construction safety programme is mostly an implementation of. It runs to 399 sections; this catalogue carries the provisions a construction health and safety programme is built on: registration and notice of project (ss. 5–7.1), project supervision and the weekly equipment inspection (ss. 13–15), personal protective equipment (ss. 21–25), fall protection (ss. 26–26.9), defibrillators (s. 27.1, added by O. Reg. 157/25), fire safety (ss. 52–58), traffic control (ss. 67–69.1), scaffolds and suspended access, elevating work platforms, cranes and rigging, electrical hazards and excavations. Consolidated to 20 April 2026, last amended by O. Reg. 116/26. Two changes are pending and are noted on the controls they affect: O. Reg. 116/26 revokes ss. 143–149 (elevating work platforms) on 1 January 2027 in favour of O. Reg. 117/26, and O. Reg. 112/26 adds side-impact and retention requirements to protective headwear on 1 July 2027.
authority: Lieutenant Governor in Council, Ontario, under the Occupational Health and Safety Act; administered by the Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development
scope: Every construction project in Ontario, and every constructor, employer, supervisor and worker at one

families.name: Registration and Notices
families.description: Sections 5 to 7.1. What must be registered, notified and posted before work begins at a project.

controls.name: Registration Form for Every Constructor and Employer
controls.description: Before beginning work at a project, each constructor and employer engaged in construction shall complete an approved registration form. The constructor shall ensure that each employer provides a completed form and that a copy is kept at the project while that employer is working there.

controls.name: Notice of Project
controls.description: Where the project meets any of the triggers in subsection 6 (1) — labour and materials expected to exceed $50,000 ($250,000 in an automobile factory), erection or structural alteration of a building over two storeys or 7.5 metres, demolition of a building at least four metres high with a floor area of at least thirty square metres, certain bridge, retaining, silo and chimney work, compressed air work, a tunnel, caisson, cofferdam or enterable well, certain trenches, an ice road, or any part required to be engineer-designed — the constructor shall file an approved notification form with the Ministry office nearest the project or submit it electronically before beginning work, and keep the completed form posted or available at the project.

controls.name: Notice of a Trench More Than 1.2 Metres Deep
controls.description: If section 6 does not apply to a project but the project includes work on a trench more than 1.2 metres deep into which a worker may enter, the constructor shall, before any work at the project begins, give notice in person, by telephone or by fax to the Ministry office nearest the project.

controls.name: Notice Before a Suspended Work Platform System is First Used
controls.description: At least 48 hours before a suspended work platform system is used for the first time at a project, the constructor shall provide an approved notification form to the Ministry office nearest the project or submit it electronically, and keep a copy in a conspicuous location at the project. Where immediate use is necessary to prevent injury or property damage, oral notice may be given first and the form provided within 24 hours of beginning to use the system.

families.name: Project Supervision and Weekly Inspection
families.description: Sections 13 to 15. The constructor's posted notice, the appointment of a supervisor and the weekly inspection of machinery and equipment.

controls.name: Constructor's Notice Posted at the Project
controls.description: A constructor shall post and keep posted at a project a notice setting out the constructor's name and business name, the address and telephone number of its head office or principal place of business in Ontario, and the address and telephone number of the nearest Ministry office. Within forty-eight hours after a health and safety representative or committee members are selected, the constructor shall add their names, trades and employers to the notice.

controls.name: Supervisor Appointed and Weekly Equipment Inspection
controls.description: A constructor shall appoint a supervisor for every project at which five or more workers will work at the same time, and the supervisor shall supervise at all times personally or through a competent assistant. The supervisor or a competent person appointed by the supervisor shall inspect all machinery and equipment — including fire extinguishing equipment, magazines, electrical installations, communication systems, sanitation and medical facilities, buildings and other structures, temporary supports and means of access and egress — at least once a week, or more often as necessary.

controls.name: Employer's Supervisor for Five or More Workers
controls.description: An employer of five or more workers on a project shall appoint a supervisor for those workers.

families.name: Protective Clothing, Equipment and Devices
families.description: Sections 21 to 25. The personal protective equipment every worker on a project must wear, and the instruction that must come with it.

controls.name: Protective Equipment Provided, Used and Instructed In
controls.description: A worker shall wear such protective clothing and use such personal protective equipment or devices as are necessary to protect the worker against the hazards to which the worker may be exposed, and the worker's employer shall require compliance. A worker required to wear or use them shall be adequately instructed and trained in their care and use before wearing or using them.

controls.name: Protective Headwear
controls.description: Every worker shall wear protective headwear at all times when on a project. The headwear shall be a safety hat with a shell and suspension adequate to protect the head against impact and against flying or falling small objects, with a shell able to withstand a dielectric strength test at 20,000 volts phase to ground. On 1 July 2027, O. Reg. 112/26 adds requirements referencing CSA Z94.1 or ANSI Z89.1, a Type 2 requirement where side impact hazards may be present, and a chin strap or other retention system where conditions may dislodge the headwear.

controls.name: Protective Footwear
controls.description: Every worker shall wear protective footwear at all times when on a project. It shall be a safety shoe or boot with a box toe adequate to protect the toes against impact and capable of resisting at least 125 joules, and with a sole or insole adequate to protect against puncture and capable of resisting a penetration load of 1.2 kilonewtons.

controls.name: Eye Protection
controls.description: A worker shall use protection appropriate in the circumstances when there is a risk of eye injury to the worker.

controls.name: Skin Protection
controls.description: A worker shall use protection appropriate in the circumstances when there is a risk of injury on a project from contact between the worker's skin and a noxious gas, liquid, fume or dust; an object that may puncture, cut or abrade the skin; a hot object, hot liquid or molten metal; or radiant heat.

families.name: Fall Protection
families.description: Sections 26 to 26.9. When fall protection is required, the ranked order of methods, the training, the guardrail specification and the rescue plan.

controls.name: When Fall Protection is Required
controls.description: Sections 26.1 to 26.9 apply where a worker may be exposed to falling more than 3 metres; falling more than 1.2 metres where the work area is a path for a wheelbarrow or similar equipment; falling into operating machinery; falling into water or another liquid; falling into or onto a hazardous substance or object; or falling through an opening on a work surface.

controls.name: Ranked Order of Fall Protection Methods
controls.description: A worker shall be adequately protected by a guardrail system meeting subsections 26.3 (2) to (8). Where that is not practicable, the worker shall be protected by the highest ranked practicable method: a travel restraint system, then a fall restricting system, then a fall arrest system, then a safety net. Components shall be designed by an engineer in accordance with good engineering practice and meet the applicable CAN/CSA Z259 standards listed in subsection 26.1 (3).

controls.name: Written Rescue Procedures Before a Fall Arrest System is Used
controls.description: Before any use of a fall arrest system or a safety net by a worker at a project, the worker's employer shall develop written procedures for rescuing the worker after a fall has been arrested.

controls.name: Training and a Signed Training Record for Fall Protection
controls.description: An employer shall ensure that a worker who may use a fall protection system is adequately trained in its use and given adequate oral and written instructions by a competent person, and that the worker also meets the working at heights training requirements of O. Reg. 297/13. The person providing the training shall prepare and sign a written training and instruction record for each worker giving the worker's name and the dates of training, and the employer shall make it available to an inspector on request.

controls.name: Guardrail Required at an Open Edge at 2.4 Metres
controls.description: Despite the 3-metre trigger in paragraph 1 of section 26, a guardrail system meeting section 26.3 shall be used where a worker has access to the perimeter or an open side of a floor (including a mezzanine or balcony), the surface of a bridge, a roof while formwork is in place, or a scaffold platform, other work platform, runway or ramp, and may be exposed to a fall of 2.4 metres or more.

controls.name: Openings in a Work Surface Protected
controls.description: One of the following shall be used to prevent a worker from falling through an opening on a work surface: a guardrail system meeting section 26.3, or a protective covering that completely covers the opening, is securely fastened, is adequately identified as covering an opening, is made from material adequate to support all loads to which it may be subjected, and can support a live load of at least 2.4 kilonewtons per square metre.

controls.name: Lanyards and Lifelines
controls.description: Where a lanyard or lifeline is part of a travel restraint system or a fall arrest system, it shall meet the requirements of section 26.9, including how it is attached, protected from chafing and abrasion, and used by no more than one worker where the section so requires.

families.name: Defibrillators
families.description: Section 27.1, added by O. Reg. 157/25. The defibrillator a project with twenty or more workers must install, maintain, sign and inspect quarterly.

controls.name: Defibrillator Installed, Maintained and Inspected Quarterly
controls.description: Where twenty or more workers are regularly employed at a project, the constructor shall ensure a Health Canada licensed defibrillator is installed and maintained, stored with the six prescribed items in a suitable, protected, labelled and unobstructed place, with signs bearing the prescribed AED symbol posted adjacent to it and elsewhere on the project. It shall be maintained and tested per the manufacturer's instructions and inspected quarterly by a competent worker, with a record kept with the defibrillator giving the date of each inspection and the name and signature of the worker. A worker trained in cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillator operation shall be present at all times when work is in progress. The section does not apply to a project expected to last less than three months.

families.name: Fire Safety
families.description: Sections 52 to 58. Fire extinguishing equipment on a project, its rating, its monthly inspection and the standpipe requirements for a building under construction.

controls.name: Fire Extinguishing Equipment Provided and Workers Trained
controls.description: Fire extinguishing equipment shall be provided at readily accessible and adequately marked locations at a project, and every worker who may be required to use it shall be trained in its use. At least one extinguisher shall be provided where flammable liquids or combustible materials are stored, handled or used; where oil-fired or gas-fired equipment other than a permanent furnace is used; where welding or open-flame operations are carried on; and on each storey of an enclosed building being constructed or altered, subject to the dwelling exemptions in subsection 52 (4).

controls.name: Fire Extinguisher Type and Rating
controls.description: Fire extinguishing equipment shall be of a suitable type and size to permit the evacuation of workers during a fire. Every fire extinguisher shall be a type whose contents are discharged under pressure and shall have an Underwriters' Laboratories of Canada rating of at least 4A40BC.

controls.name: Fire Extinguishing Equipment Protected and Recharged
controls.description: Fire extinguishing equipment shall be protected from physical damage and from freezing, and after a fire extinguisher is used it shall be refilled or replaced immediately.

controls.name: Monthly Fire Extinguisher Inspection Recorded on a Tag
controls.description: Every fire extinguisher shall be inspected for defects or deterioration at least once a month by a competent worker, who shall record the date of the inspection on a tag attached to it.

controls.name: Standpipe Kept Within Two Storeys of the Work Level
controls.description: As construction proceeds in a building with two or more storeys, a permanent or temporary standpipe shall be installed such that the distance between the standpipe and the uppermost work level is no more than two storeys at any time, unless the building is not required by the Building Code to have a permanent standpipe. The section sets the hose outlet, fire department connection, hose and nozzle requirements, and requires that a temporary standpipe not be disconnected until the permanent one is connected.

families.name: Traffic Control
families.description: Sections 67 to 69.1. Protecting workers from vehicular traffic, the written traffic protection plan, the sign a traffic control person uses and the competency that person must have.

controls.name: Measures Against Vehicular Traffic
controls.description: If a worker at a project on a highway may be endangered by vehicular traffic unrelated to the project, the project shall make use of as many of the listed measures as is necessary to adequately protect the worker: barriers, barricades, delineators, lane control devices, warning signs, flashing lights, flares, traffic control devices, blocker trucks, crash trucks, sign trucks, speed control devices and longitudinal buffer areas.

controls.name: Written Traffic Protection Plan
controls.description: Every employer shall develop in writing and implement a traffic protection plan for the employer's workers at a project if any of them may be exposed to a hazard from vehicular traffic. The plan shall specify the traffic hazards and the measures in subsection 67 (2) to be used, and shall be kept at the project and made available to an inspector or a worker on request.

controls.name: Competent Worker Sets Up and Removes Traffic Measures
controls.description: A worker required to set up or remove traffic protection measures on a roadway or its shoulder shall be a competent worker, shall not perform any other work while doing so, and shall be given adequate written and oral instructions, in a language the worker understands, on setting up or removing the measures.

controls.name: Barriers on a Freeway Project Over Five Days
controls.description: Adequate barriers shall be installed to protect workers at a project that is on a freeway, is not a mobile operation and is expected to require more than five days to complete. Where barriers are not practical, or the project is expected to take five days or less, crash trucks shall be adequately positioned instead.

controls.name: Traffic Control Sign Specification
controls.description: A sign used by a worker to direct vehicular traffic shall be octagonal, 450 millimetres between opposite sides, mounted on a 1.2-metre pole, made of material at least as rigid as six-millimetre plywood, red retro-reflective with white "STOP" lettering 150 millimetres high on one side and fluorescent chartreuse micro-prismatic with a black diamond border and black "SLOW" lettering 120 millimetres high on the other, and maintained clean and legible.

controls.name: Directing Traffic on a Public Way
controls.description: Where vehicular traffic on a public way may be a hazard to workers, a worker shall not direct traffic for more than one lane in the same direction, and section 69 sets the further conditions and protective clothing requirements that apply to directing traffic.

families.name: Scaffolds and Suspended Access
families.description: Sections 126 to 142.8. Scaffold design and loading, and the training and competency required before a suspended work platform or boatswain's chair is used or installed.

controls.name: Scaffold Design and Loading
controls.description: Every scaffold shall be designed and constructed to support or resist two times the maximum load or force to which it is likely to be subjected without exceeding allowable unit stresses, and four times that load without overturning. A scaffold whose component capacity can only be determined by testing shall support or resist three times the maximum load without component failure. No scaffold shall be loaded beyond what it was designed and constructed to bear.

controls.name: Training Before a Suspended Work Platform or Boatswain's Chair is Used
controls.description: An employer shall ensure that a worker successfully completes a training program meeting the requirements of subsection 138 (2) before the worker uses a suspended work platform system or boatswain's chair for the first time, and thereafter at the intervals the section sets.

controls.name: Competent Worker Designated for Installation and Inspection
controls.description: An employer shall designate a competent worker to be responsible for the installation and inspection of a suspended work platform system or boatswain's chair before it is put into service for the first time, and shall ensure that worker successfully completes a training program meeting subsection 138.1 (3) before installing or inspecting such an installation for the first time and thereafter as the section requires.

families.name: Elevating Work Platforms
families.description: Sections 143 to 149. Design, maintenance records, operator instruction and the manual kept with the machine. NOTE: O. Reg. 116/26 revokes sections 143 to 149 on 1 January 2027, when O. Reg. 117/26 (Elevating Work Platforms) takes their place.

controls.name: Elevating Work Platform Design
controls.description: An elevating work platform shall be designed by an engineer in accordance with good engineering practice to meet the applicable National Standards of Canada standard set out in the Table to subsection 144 (6) and to support a minimum 1.3 kilonewton rated working load determined in accordance with that standard. Revoked 1 January 2027 by O. Reg. 116/26.

controls.name: Maintenance and a Permanent Record of Inspections
controls.description: The owner of an elevating work platform shall maintain it such that the safety factors of the original design are maintained, and shall keep a permanent record of all inspections, tests, repairs, modifications and maintenance performed on it. Revoked 1 January 2027 by O. Reg. 116/26.

controls.name: Operator Instruction and Training Before First Use
controls.description: A worker who operates an elevating work platform shall, before using it for the first time, be given oral and written instruction on the operation and be trained to operate that class of elevating work platform, covering the matters listed in subsection 147 (2). Revoked 1 January 2027 by O. Reg. 116/26.

controls.name: Operator's Manual Kept With the Machine
controls.description: An operator's manual for an elevating work platform shall be kept with it while it is on a project. Revoked 1 January 2027 by O. Reg. 116/26.

families.name: Cranes, Hoisting and Rigging
families.description: Sections 149.1 to 180. Who may operate a crane, its rated capacity, the owner's crane log and the weekly inspection of cables.

controls.name: Crane Operator Certificate of Qualification
controls.description: No worker shall operate a crane or similar hoisting device unless the worker holds an unsuspended certificate of qualification or provisional certificate issued under the Building Opportunities in the Skilled Trades Act, 2021, or is a registered apprentice, in the trade of hoisting engineer — mobile crane operator 1, hoisting engineer — mobile crane operator 2 or hoisting engineer — tower crane operator, as the capacity and type of the device require.

controls.name: Rated Load-Carrying Capacity Not Exceeded
controls.description: No crane or similar hoisting device shall be subjected to a load greater than its rated load-carrying capacity, other than during load tests required by the manufacturer. The manufacturer or an engineer shall determine the rated load-carrying capacity in accordance with the applicable CSA standard.

controls.name: Owner's Crane Log
controls.description: The owner of a crane or similar hoisting device shall keep an owner's crane log consisting of a record of all inspections, tests, repairs, modifications and maintenance. Where the log does not contain all the required information, the owner shall ensure an inspection meeting clause 6.4.7 of CSA Z248-17 (tower cranes) or clause 5.3.5 of CSA Z150-16 (mobile cranes) is completed before the crane is put into service at a project.

controls.name: Weekly Visual Inspection of Crane Cables
controls.description: All cables used by a crane or other hoisting device shall be visually inspected by a competent worker at least once a week when the crane or hoisting device is being used, or more frequently if the cable manufacturer recommends it. The worker shall record the condition of the cable inspected, and the record shall be kept at the project while the crane or hoisting device is in use there.

families.name: Electrical Hazards
families.description: Sections 181 to 195.3. Who may work on electrical equipment, the minimum distances from energized overhead conductors, and what applies when work on energized parts cannot be avoided.

controls.name: Electrical Utility Safety Rules
controls.description: Except where otherwise required by the Regulation, electrical work performed on or near electrical transmission or distribution systems shall be performed in accordance with the Electrical Utility Safety Rules published by the Infrastructure Health and Safety Association, revised 2019. Where work is performed in accordance with that document, sections 182, 187, 188, 189, 190, 191 and 193 do not apply.

controls.name: Certificate of Qualification for Electrical Work
controls.description: No worker shall connect, maintain or modify electrical equipment or installations unless the worker holds an unsuspended certificate of qualification or provisional certificate under the Building Opportunities in the Skilled Trades Act, 2021 in the trade of electrician — construction and maintenance, or electrician — domestic and rural within that trade's scope of practice, or is otherwise permitted under that Act.

controls.name: Minimum Distance From Energized Overhead Conductors
controls.description: No object shall be brought closer to an energized overhead electrical conductor than the distance specified in the Table to subsection 188 (2) for the conductor's nominal phase-to-phase voltage rating, unless the conditions in clauses 189 (a) and (b) are satisfied.

controls.name: Work on or Near Energized Exposed Parts
controls.description: Where it is not reasonably possible to disconnect equipment, an installation or a conductor from the power supply before working on or near energized exposed parts, section 191 applies instead of section 190 and sets the precautions, insulating protection and procedures required.

families.name: Excavations
families.description: Part III, sections 222 to 242. Soil classification, the condition of the excavation, and the support system that must protect its walls.

controls.name: Soil Type Determined by Examination
controls.description: The type of soil in which an excavation is made shall be determined by visual and physical examination of the soil at the walls of the excavation and within the excavation's zone of influence, in accordance with section 227.

controls.name: Excavation Kept Free of Water
controls.description: Every excavation that a worker may be required to enter shall be kept reasonably free of water.

controls.name: Spoil, Equipment and Barriers at the Edge
controls.description: A level area extending at least one metre from the upper edge of each wall of an excavation shall be kept clear of equipment, excavated soil, rock and construction material; the stability of a wall shall be maintained where stockpiling may affect it; no vehicle or machine shall be operated or located so as to affect the stability of a wall; and where a person could fall into an excavation more than 2.4 metres deep, a barrier at least 1.1 metres high shall be provided at the top of every wall that is not sloped as clauses 234 (2) (e), (f) and (g) describe.

controls.name: Support System Required Unless an Exemption Applies
controls.description: The walls of an excavation shall be supported by a support system complying with sections 235 to 241, unless the excavation is less than 1.2 metres deep, no worker is required to enter it, it is not a trench and no worker need be closer to a wall than the wall's height, it is cut in sound and stable rock, its walls are sloped as prescribed for the soil type, or an engineer has given a written opinion that the walls are sufficiently stable. The constructor shall keep a copy of every such engineer's opinion on the project while it is in progress, and the engineer or a competent worker the engineer designates shall inspect the excavation as frequently as the opinion specifies.

controls.name: Composition of the Support System
controls.description: A support system shall consist of timbering and shoring meeting subsection 238 (2) where no hydrostatic pressure is present and the excavation is within the Table to section 238; a prefabricated support system complying with sections 236 and 237; a hydraulic support system complying with sections 236 and 237; or an engineered support system complying with section 236. Where the excavation is a trench deeper than six metres or wider than 3.6 metres, the support system shall be an engineered support system designed for the specific location and project.

controls.name: Prefabricated, Hydraulic and Engineered Support Systems Designed by an Engineer
controls.description: Every prefabricated, hydraulic or engineered support system shall be designed by an engineer, and section 236 sets what the design and its documentation shall establish and what shall be kept at the project.
